description: Multiple GROUP BY super-group elements combine as a CROSS PRODUCT of their grouping sets, not a flat union. ROLLUP(a), ROLLUP(g) is the grouping sets {(a,g),(a),(g),()} - not {(a),(),(g),()}, which duplicated the grand total and dropped the (a,g) detail rows. Over a three-row fixture that is 3 detail rows plus 2 for (a), 2 for (g) and exactly one grand total: eight rows. Converted 1:1 from query/GroupByCrossProductTest (now retired); the Java counted rows and then counted how many carried the grand total's sum, which would also have accepted the right count of the wrong rows - the converted test states all eight rows and their keys, so the (a,g) detail rows are named rather than inferred from a count.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE gt (a VARCHAR, g VARCHAR, v INTEGER)
SELECT a, g, SUM(v) FROM gt GROUP BY ROLLUP(a), ROLLUP(g) ORDER BY a NULLS LAST, g NULLS LAST
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT a, g, SUM(v) AS s FROM gt GROUP BY ROLLUP(a), ROLLUP(g)) WHERE a IS NULL AND g IS NULL
